failure_summary.description: Added unsupported refinements or exceptions, or weakened a literal theorem bound, based on plausibility rather than the exact result.
Confused distinct algebraic claims or criteria and relied on terminology or remembered formulations instead of checking their exact scope.
Confused uniqueness of the minimizing object with uniqueness only up to its induced degeneration.

patch.reasoning: The main recurring gap is not lack of general caution but failing to apply it when options differ by endpoints, constants, sharper bounds, exceptions, or uniqueness. Add an operational reminder to verify each such clause independently and to distinguish objects from equivalence classes.

edits.target: - For an equivalence, check both implications.
edits.content: - For a “strongest” or “complete characterization” question, verify each refinement against the exact result: a theorem valid on a stated parameter range does not establish failure outside it, and do not insert a conventional constant that weakens an explicitly normalized bound. Distinguish uniqueness of an object from uniqueness up to isomorphism, scaling, or induced data. When options give different algebraic criteria, check whether they are actually equivalent in the stated class; use small admissible examples to separate them rather than choosing by terminology.
